mechanisms.name: `privateKey.rotationPolicy` default `Never` -> `Always` (gate `DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways`)
resourcesConsumers: checkout consumer (checkout-deployment.yaml, curl loop every 30s reading /tls/tls.crt and /tls/tls.key)
any key pinning / systems recording the leaf public key (SPKI pins, allowlists, HSM or audit records) — none found in repo

mechanisms.mechanism: The default flips to `Always` in the controller (not the CRD schema), so ledger-tls and checkout-tls, which set no `rotationPolicy`, switch from reusing the key to generating a new key on every re-issuance (about every 20 days with duration 720h / renewBefore 240h). Nothing happens at upgrade time; the first rotation lands up to 20 days after the upgrade, so a clean post-upgrade check proves nothing. For checkout, curl opens cert and key as two separate file opens, so a read that straddles the kubelet symlink swap could pair the new cert with the old key; expected to cost at most one failed 30s iteration ("ledger call failed"), not tested. Real consumers with a similar read pattern would be worse. For ledger, nginx only loads cert/key at start or reload and no reloader exists, so it keeps serving the old pair until restart; this is already true today (latent problem: renewal day 20, expiry day 30). Rotation does not make that worse but means a restart after renewal loads an entirely new keypair. Any key pinning or system recording the leaf public key would break on rotation. Described as Medium severity: not an outage by itself, but adds a race for the mTLS consumers.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Preferred: in a PR before the upgrade, set `privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never` or `Always` explicitly on ledger-certificate.yaml and checkout-certificate.yaml (required anyway before 1.19 removes the gate); for a payments mTLS mesh, key rotation is probably desirable, so if so pick `Always` explicitly and fix the reload gap first. Alternative: set `config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false` in platform/cert-manager/values.yaml as a temporary hold, which only defers the decision to 1.19. No key pinning exists in the repo, but only an engineer can confirm there are no out-of-band consumers.
